title: Social Science (EVS in Classes 1-5)
topics: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
syllabus: unverified: topics are the drafting model’s reading of the official syllabus (NCERT/CBSE, or the exam’s notified syllabus) and have not been checked against the official documents

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which period of the Stone Age is known for the earliest use of rough, chipped stone tools?
questions.explanation: The Palaeolithic or Old Stone Age is the earliest period, when people used roughly chipped stone tools.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these was a key feature of the Neolithic period?
options: Beginning of farming and settled village life
questions.explanation: The Neolithic is associated with the start of agriculture, animal rearing and settled villages.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The ancient Mesopotamian civilisation grew up between which two rivers?
questions.explanation: Mesopotamia means 'land between the rivers', the Tigris and the Euphrates.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which is a likely reason early farming communities began to live in permanent villages?
options: They had no need for water
They wanted to avoid all trade
Crops needed care between sowing and harvest
questions.explanation: Growing crops requires staying near the fields from sowing to harvest, which encouraged settled life.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Early cities in river valleys are linked to agricultural surplus. Which result of surplus best explains the rise of crafts and administration?
options: Some people were freed from farming to do other work
Everyone had to move to the hills
questions.explanation: When farmers produced more than they needed, others could specialise as artisans, traders, priests and officials.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: For prehistoric periods historians depend mostly on material remains such as tools and bones because
options: people in those times did not exist
no written records exist from those times
questions.explanation: Writing had not yet developed, so objects found by archaeologists are the main evidence.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is meant by a hunter-gatherer way of life?
questions.answer: It is a way of life in which people got food by hunting animals, fishing and collecting wild fruits, roots and seeds, and moved from place to place instead of farming.
keyPoints: mostly moved from place to place
questions.explanation: Hunter-gatherers depended directly on what nature provided and generally did not live in permanent settlements.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the invention of writing important for the study of ancient civilisations?
questions.answer: Writing allowed records of laws, trade, taxes and events to be kept, so historians can read direct evidence about how people lived, instead of only guessing from objects.
keyPoints: records of trade, laws and events
helps administration and passing on knowledge
questions.explanation: Written records give historians richer and more precise information than material remains alone.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which city was the centre of the ancient Roman Empire?
questions.explanation: Rome was the capital and heart of the Roman state.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who is regarded as the first emperor of Rome?
questions.explanation: Augustus, formerly Octavian, became the first Roman emperor after the Republic ended.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Hijra, the migration of Prophet Muhammad from Mecca to Medina, took place in which year?
questions.explanation: The Hijra occurred in 622 CE, which marks the start of the Islamic calendar.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Western Roman Empire is traditionally said to have ended in
questions.explanation: The deposition of the last western emperor in 476 CE is the traditional date.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A large empire needed good roads. Which was the most important administrative benefit of such roads?
options: They ended the need for taxes
Faster movement of troops, officials and messages
questions.explanation: Roads let rulers send armies and orders quickly and keep distant provinces under control.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Empires that expanded very quickly often found it hard to rule distant provinces. Which would most help hold such an empire together?
options: A common system of law, taxes and communication
questions.explanation: Shared laws, regular taxation and communication links create a common framework of control.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Describe two ways in which the Roman state ruled its large empire.
questions.answer: Rome used a professional army to defend and control provinces, and appointed governors to collect taxes and keep order. It also built roads and applied Roman law.
questions.explanation: Military power, officials and communication links together held the empire.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain with an example why long-distance trade routes spread ideas as well as goods.
questions.answer: Merchants and travellers moving along routes such as the Silk Road met many peoples, so religions, techniques and customs travelled with their goods. Buddhism, for example, spread across Central Asia to China along such routes.
keyPoints: ideas and religions travelled with goods
example such as Silk Road and Buddhism
questions.explanation: Contact through trade carried culture and knowledge across regions.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In which country did the Renaissance begin?
questions.explanation: The Renaissance began in Italian cities such as Florence and Venice.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci, a leading Renaissance artist and thinker, painted the Mona Lisa.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who is credited with introducing the movable-type printing press in Europe around the middle of the fifteenth century?
questions.explanation: Johannes Gutenberg of Germany developed movable-type printing in Europe.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Martin Luther began his criticism of Church practices in 1517 in which region?
questions.explanation: Luther, a German monk, started the Reformation in 1517 in the German lands.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How did the printing press help spread Renaissance and Reformation ideas?
options: It made books cheaper so ideas reached many more readers
It replaced every school at once
questions.explanation: Printing lowered the cost of books and pamphlets and let ideas travel quickly and widely.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A thinker who stresses the study of classical Greek and Roman texts and the worth of human achievement is expressing which Renaissance idea?
questions.explanation: Humanism focused on human potential and revived classical learning.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name any two changes brought about by the Industrial Revolution in Britain.
questions.answer: It brought factory production using machines and steam power, and it caused rapid growth of towns as people moved from villages to work. It also created new classes of factory owners and workers.
questions.explanation: Machine production changed where and how people worked and lived.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how the French Revolution of 1789 spread the ideas of liberty and equality.
questions.answer: The revolution ended the absolute monarchy and declared the rights of citizens with the slogan of liberty, equality and fraternity. These ideas were widely discussed and inspired demands for change in other countries.
questions.explanation: The revolution made equal rights and popular sovereignty central political ideas.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which layer of the Earth is the outermost solid layer?
questions.explanation: The crust is the thin, solid outer layer on which we live.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which type of rock is formed by the cooling and solidification of molten magma or lava?
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form when molten material cools and hardens.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Granite is an example of
questions.explanation: Granite cools slowly below the surface, making it an intrusive igneous rock.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Marble is formed by the transformation of which rock?
questions.explanation: Heat and pressure change limestone into marble, a metamorphic rock.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why do scientists learn about the Earth's interior mostly from seismic waves rather than by drilling?
options: Seismic waves are made of light
The interior is too deep and hot to reach, and waves change speed and path in different materials
questions.explanation: The deepest boreholes reach only a tiny part of the crust, so waves from earthquakes reveal the layers.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Sandstone often shows distinct layers because
options: sediments were deposited in layers and later compacted
questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks form as sediments settle in successive layers and are cemented.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Distinguish between P-waves and S-waves.
questions.answer: P-waves are primary compressional waves that travel faster and pass through solids and liquids. S-waves are slower, move particles at right angles to their direction, and cannot pass through liquids.
keyPoints: P-waves travel through solids and liquids
questions.explanation: The S-wave shadow zone showed that part of the Earth's core is liquid.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how the movement of plates can lead to earthquakes and volcanoes.
questions.answer: Plates move slowly and where they collide, separate or slide past one another, stress builds up in rocks. Sudden release of this stress causes earthquakes, and where molten magma rises through weak zones, volcanoes form.
keyPoints: stress builds and is released as earthquakes
magma rises at weak zones forming volcanoes
questions.explanation: Most earthquakes and volcanoes occur along plate boundaries.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which gas is the most abundant in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78 per cent of dry air.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In which layer of the atmosphere does most weather occur?
questions.explanation: The troposphere, the lowest layer, holds most water vapour and clouds.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The ozone layer is found mainly in the
questions.explanation: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere and absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which instrument measures atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures air pressure.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is it generally colder at the top of a high mountain than at its base?
options: Temperature in the troposphere generally falls with height
The Sun never shines at the top
Wind is always absent at the top
questions.explanation: The normal lapse rate is a fall of temperature with increasing altitude in the troposphere.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Coastal places usually have a smaller range of temperature than interior places mainly because
options: water heats and cools more slowly than land
the Sun shines less at the coast
coasts are always at high altitude
questions.explanation: The sea moderates temperatures because water has a high heat capacity.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name the layers of the atmosphere in order from the Earth's surface upward.
questions.answer: Troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere.
keyPoints: thermosphere and exosphere at the top
questions.explanation: The layers are based mainly on how temperature changes with height.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how ocean currents influence the climate of nearby coastal regions.
questions.answer: Warm currents raise temperatures and bring moisture to coasts they flow along, while cold currents lower temperatures and often make coasts drier. Currents therefore make coastal climates different from places at the same latitude inland.
questions.explanation: Currents carry heat across the oceans and shape coastal weather.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The variety of living organisms on Earth is called
questions.explanation: Biodiversity means the variety of life forms in an area or on Earth.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: By which process do green plants make food using sunlight?
questions.explanation: In photosynthesis, plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which soil layer is usually the topmost and richest in humus?
questions.explanation: The uppermost layer, topsoil, contains most of the organic matter.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Mangrove forests are best suited to
questions.explanation: Mangroves grow in tidal, salty coastal areas and river deltas.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the clearing of forests a concern for biodiversity?
options: Trees are not used by animals
Forests have no link to soil
It removes habitats on which many species depend
questions.explanation: Many plants and animals live only in forests, so losing them threatens species.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Heavy rain is more likely to erode bare slopes than forested slopes because
options: roots and leaf cover bind soil and slow the water
questions.explanation: Plant roots hold soil and leaves reduce the force of falling rain.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is an ecosystem? Give one example.
questions.answer: An ecosystem is a community of living organisms interacting with one another and with their non-living surroundings such as air, water and soil. A pond or a forest is an example.
keyPoints: example such as pond or forest
questions.explanation: Ecosystems link organisms and their physical environment.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how parent rock, climate and living organisms influence soil formation.
questions.answer: Weathering of the parent rock supplies the mineral particles of the soil. Climate, through temperature and rainfall, controls the speed of weathering, while plants, animals and microbes add humus and mix the soil.
questions.explanation: Soil is the product of rock, climate, living things and time acting together.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Himalayas are an example of which type of mountains?
questions.explanation: The Himalayas are young fold mountains formed by collision of plates.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which is the longest river of peninsular India?
questions.explanation: The Godavari is the longest river of the peninsular plateau.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these rivers flows westward into the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: The Narmada flows through a rift valley and empties into the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Most of India's annual rainfall arrives during which months?
questions.explanation: The southwest monsoon brings most of India's rainfall between June and September.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are the northern plains of India very suitable for agriculture?
options: Rivers deposited fertile alluvium on level land
They are covered by volcanic lava
questions.explanation: Alluvial soil, flat land and water from rivers support intensive farming.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Himalayan rivers carry water through the year, while many peninsular rivers swell mostly in the monsoon. Why?
options: Himalayan rivers are fed by snow melt as well as rain
The Ganga flows only in winter
questions.explanation: Glaciers and snowfields feed Himalayan rivers, whereas peninsular rivers depend on rain.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name any four physiographic divisions of India.
questions.answer: The Himalayan mountains, the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands.
questions.explanation: India's relief is commonly divided into these major regions.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the monsoon important to Indian agriculture, and why does its variability matter?
questions.answer: A large part of Indian farming depends on monsoon rain for water. If the rain is late, weak or excessive, crops fail or are damaged, so farmers' incomes and food production are affected.
questions.explanation: Rainfall variation can cause drought or floods and affects the rural economy.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India?
questions.explanation: Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Constitution of India came into effect on
questions.explanation: It came into force on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected President of the Constituent Assembly.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution begins with the words
questions.explanation: The Preamble opens with 'We, the people of India', showing the source of authority.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why does a democracy need a Constitution that is not easy for a government to change at will?
options: To protect basic principles from short-term majorities
questions.explanation: A rigid core keeps basic rights and the structure of government secure from passing majorities.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 but enforced on 26 January 1950. The choice of that date is linked to
questions.explanation: 26 January had been observed as Independence Day after the Purna Swaraj resolution of the Congress.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name any two features that the Indian Constitution borrowed from other countries, with the source.
questions.answer: The parliamentary system of government was drawn from Britain, and the Fundamental Rights were inspired by the Constitution of the United States. The Directive Principles drew on the Irish Constitution.
questions.explanation: The framers adapted ideas from several constitutions to Indian needs.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is a Constitution needed in a democracy? Give two reasons.
questions.answer: A Constitution lays down how power is shared and used, so that rulers cannot act arbitrarily. It also protects the rights of citizens and sets out the basic rules on which society agrees to be governed.
questions.explanation: A Constitution provides trust and coordination among citizens and a check on rulers.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Right to Life and Personal Liberty is found in
questions.explanation: Article 21 protects life and personal liberty.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Article 14 of the Constitution guarantees
options: equality before law and equal protection of the laws
questions.explanation: Article 14 is the basic guarantee of equality before the law.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which writ is issued to produce a detained person before a court?
questions.explanation: Habeas corpus means 'you may have the body' and protects against unlawful detention.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Dr Ambedkar called Article 32 the heart and soul of the Constitution because it
options: lets citizens approach the Supreme Court directly to enforce Fundamental Rights
creates the post of Prime Minister
questions.explanation: The right to constitutional remedies makes the other rights enforceable.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which statement best describes secularism in the Indian constitutional context?
options: The State has one official religion
The State has no official religion and treats all religions fairly
Religion is banned in public life
Only the majority religion is protected
questions.explanation: India's secular State does not favour any religion and guarantees freedom of religion.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: List the six categories of Fundamental Rights originally given in the Constitution.
questions.answer: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies. The Right to Property was originally the seventh.
questions.explanation: The Right to Property was later removed from the list of Fundamental Rights.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why should rights be accompanied by duties? Explain with an example.
questions.answer: One person's exercise of a right must not harm the rights of others, so citizens must respect the law and others' freedoms. For example, the right to free speech does not allow spreading false statements that harm another person.
keyPoints: rights of one must not harm others
questions.explanation: Rights and duties together make it possible for all to enjoy freedom.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Parliament of India consists of the President and
options: the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha
questions.explanation: Parliament has two Houses, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, along with the President.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Real executive power in the parliamentary system at the Centre is held by
options: the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister
questions.explanation: The President is the nominal head, while the Council of Ministers exercises real power.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who presides over the sittings of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The Speaker chairs the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The minimum age to be a member of the Lok Sabha is
questions.explanation: A person must be at least 25 to contest for the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the Council of Ministers said to be collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha?
options: It is chosen by the Rajya Sabha
The government must keep the confidence of the Lok Sabha majority or resign
questions.explanation: If the Lok Sabha withdraws its support, the entire ministry must leave office.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is an independent judiciary important in a federal democracy?
options: It makes laws for the country
It settles disputes between governments and protects rights without pressure
questions.explanation: An independent court can interpret the Constitution and check the government fairly.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Mention two functions of the Election Commission of India.
questions.answer: The Election Commission supervises and conducts elections to Parliament, State legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President. It also prepares and updates the electoral rolls.
questions.explanation: The Commission is an independent constitutional body.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Compare the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha on any two points.
questions.answer: Members of the Lok Sabha are directly elected by the people, whereas Rajya Sabha members are mostly elected indirectly by State legislators. The Lok Sabha has a normal term of five years, but the Rajya Sabha is a permanent House with one-third of its members retiring every two years.
keyPoints: Rajya Sabha is permanent, one-third retire every two years
questions.explanation: The two Houses differ in composition, term and powers.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Which concept means the absence of unjust restraints on what individuals may do?
questions.explanation: Freedom, or liberty, is the absence of unjust constraints.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: The French Revolution slogan of 1789 was liberty, equality and
questions.explanation: The slogan was liberty, equality and fraternity.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Giving every adult citizen one vote of equal value is an example of
questions.explanation: Equal voting rights are a form of political equality.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: A special measure to help historically disadvantaged groups is often justified as promoting
questions.explanation: Supporters argue that such measures correct past disadvantage and promote social justice.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: John Rawls' idea of the 'veil of ignorance' asks people to design the rules of society
options: without knowing what position they will hold in it
questions.explanation: Not knowing their future position, people would choose rules fair to everyone.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Why is treating everyone in exactly the same way not always fair?
options: Because laws should never apply to anyone
Because people may have different needs and starting points
questions.explanation: Fair treatment sometimes needs attention to relevant differences between people.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Distinguish between negative and positive liberty.
questions.answer: Negative liberty means the absence of external restraints or interference on a person. Positive liberty means having the capacity and conditions, such as education and health, to develop and act on one's choices.
keyPoints: positive: capacity and conditions to act
questions.explanation: The two ideas describe freedom as non-interference and as the ability to achieve one's aims.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Explain how inequality of wealth can limit political equality even when everyone has one vote.
questions.answer: Wealthier people may have more resources to spend on campaigns, publicity and access to decision-makers, so they can influence politics more than the poor. Equal votes may then not give equal influence.
questions.explanation: Political equality is easier to achieve when economic gaps are not very wide.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Five Year Plans in India were drawn up by which body?
questions.explanation: The Planning Commission prepared the Five Year Plans.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The economic reforms of liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation began in India in the year
questions.explanation: A major reform programme began in 1991 after a balance of payments crisis.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: India's first Five Year Plan began in
questions.explanation: The First Five Year Plan covered 1951 to 1956 and stressed agriculture.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Green Revolution mainly increased the production of
questions.explanation: High-yielding seeds, fertiliser and irrigation raised wheat and rice output.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did the Second Five Year Plan stress heavy industry?
options: To increase imports of consumer goods
To build an industrial base and reduce dependence on imported capital goods
questions.explanation: The aim was to make machines and steel at home and support long-term growth.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Land reforms such as the abolition of intermediaries aimed mainly to
options: reduce inequality and give cultivators direct rights over land
questions.explanation: Removing intermediaries was meant to benefit actual cultivators and improve productivity.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is meant by liberalisation of the economy?
questions.answer: Liberalisation means reducing government controls and restrictions on industry, trade and investment, such as licences and high import duties, so that private firms can operate and compete more freely.
keyPoints: removal of licences and trade barriers
questions.explanation: It was a key element of the 1991 reforms.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Give two possible benefits and one concern of opening an economy to foreign trade.
questions.answer: Benefits include access to wider markets and technology, and more choice and competition for consumers. A concern is that small domestic producers may find it hard to compete with large foreign firms.
questions.explanation: Trade opening has both gains and adjustment costs.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The arithmetic mean of 2, 4, 6 and 8 is
questions.explanation: The sum is 20 and 20 divided by 4 is 5.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The middle value of a data set arranged in order is called the
questions.explanation: The median is the middle item of an ordered series.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The mode of the data 3, 5, 5, 7, 5, 9 is
questions.explanation: The mode is the most frequent value, which is 5.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The median of 3, 7, 9, 12 and 15 is
questions.explanation: With five values in order, the third value, 9, is the median.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The median is often preferred to the mean when data contain extreme values because
options: extreme values affect the mean much more than the median
the median ignores the middle item
questions.explanation: A few very large or small values can pull the mean away from the typical value.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A student visits ten shops to note prices herself, while her friend copies prices from a published report. Which statement is correct?
options: The student has used primary data and her friend secondary data
The student has used secondary data and her friend primary data
questions.explanation: First-hand collected data are primary; data already published by others are secondary.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is a census, and how does it differ from a sample survey?
questions.answer: A census collects information from every unit of the population, while a sample survey collects it from only a selected part of the population. A census is more complete but costlier and slower.
keyPoints: census costs more time and money
questions.explanation: The choice depends on cost, time and the accuracy required.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is sampling often used instead of a complete enumeration?
questions.answer: Studying every item can be too costly, slow or even impossible, for example if testing destroys the item. A properly chosen sample can give reliable results quickly at lower cost.
keyPoints: a representative sample gives reliable results
questions.explanation: Sampling works well only when the sample represents the population.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these was a major city of the Harappan (Indus Valley) civilisation?
questions.explanation: Mohenjo-daro and Harappa were two of the best-known Indus cities.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which ancient civilisation built pyramids as royal tombs?
questions.explanation: The pyramids were built in ancient Egypt as tombs for pharaohs.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Great Bath was found at which Harappan site?
questions.explanation: The Great Bath is a famous structure at Mohenjo-daro.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Ancient Egyptian writing that used picture signs is known as
questions.explanation: Hieroglyphics were the picture-based script of ancient Egypt.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Harappan towns had streets laid out in a grid and covered drains. What does this most strongly suggest?
questions.explanation: Such layouts need planning and some authority to maintain them.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the Harappan script a challenge for historians?
options: It has not yet been deciphered
questions.explanation: Scholars have not been able to read the script, so much about Harappan society is learnt from objects.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why was the River Nile so important to ancient Egyptian civilisation?
questions.answer: The Nile's yearly flood left fertile silt on its banks, so farmers could grow good crops in an otherwise dry land. The river was also a route for transport and trade.
questions.explanation: Egypt is often described as the gift of the Nile.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How do seals and weights found at Harappan sites suggest the existence of trade?
questions.answer: Seals were probably used to mark goods or bundles of goods, and standard weights suggest goods were measured in a uniform way. Seals found in Mesopotamia show that traders also dealt with distant lands.
questions.explanation: Standard measures and distant finds point to organised long-distance exchange.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Quran is the holy book of which religion?
questions.explanation: The Quran is the sacred book of Islam.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who founded the Mongol empire in the early thirteenth century?
questions.explanation: Genghis Khan united the Mongol tribes and founded the empire.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The successors of Prophet Muhammad as leaders of the Muslim community were called
questions.explanation: The leaders after the Prophet were known as caliphs.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In medieval Europe, which system had lords grant land to vassals in return for loyalty and service?
questions.explanation: This land-for-service arrangement is called feudalism.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How did the growth of towns and trade in Europe weaken feudal society?
options: Merchants and townspeople gained wealth and some freedom outside the manor system
questions.explanation: Town life and money trade offered alternatives to dependence on a lord.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Peasants in feudal Europe had limited chances to improve their position mainly because
options: they were bound to the manor and owed labour and dues to the lord
questions.explanation: Serfs were tied to the land and had to work and pay for the lord.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What was a manor in medieval Europe?
questions.answer: A manor was the estate of a lord, including his house, fields, pasture and village. Peasants cultivated its land and gave the lord labour and a share of produce.
keyPoints: labour and dues owed to the lord
questions.explanation: The manor was the basic unit of the rural economy under feudalism.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Mongol conquests are described as both destructive and connecting. Explain this statement.
questions.answer: Conquests caused great loss of life and destroyed cities. However, the large empire also brought many regions under one rule, making trade and travel across Eurasia easier and spreading ideas and technology.
keyPoints: destruction of cities and loss of life
easier trade and exchange of ideas
questions.explanation: The same conquests that caused destruction also linked distant regions.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Industrial Revolution began in which country?
questions.explanation: Britain was the first country to industrialise, from the later eighteenth century.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who proposed that the Earth and other planets move around the Sun?
questions.explanation: Nicolaus Copernicus put forward the Sun-centred model.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The American Declaration of Independence was adopted in
questions.explanation: The Declaration was adopted by the thirteen colonies in 1776.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: James Watt is best known for improving the
questions.explanation: Watt's improvements made the steam engine far more efficient.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Industrial Revolution led to fast growth of cities mainly because
questions.explanation: People moved from villages to factory towns in search of work.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How did Enlightenment thinkers' stress on reason challenge absolute monarchy?
options: They argued kings were always right
They argued authority should rest on reason and the consent of the people, not divine right
They wanted to end all laws
questions.explanation: Ideas of reason and consent undermined the claim that kings ruled by divine right.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is meant by the Reformation in European history?
questions.answer: The Reformation was a sixteenth-century movement that began as a call to reform the Roman Catholic Church and led to the rise of Protestant churches.
questions.explanation: It began with Martin Luther's challenge in 1517 and spread across Europe.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain why industrialising countries of Europe looked for colonies.
questions.answer: Factories needed cheap raw materials such as cotton and also needed markets in which to sell their goods. Colonies could supply raw materials and buy manufactured goods, and offered places to invest.
questions.explanation: Industrial growth increased demand for resources and markets overseas.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The breaking down of rocks in place by natural agents is called
questions.explanation: Weathering breaks rock where it stands, without moving it away.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which is the highest mountain peak above sea level on Earth?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest in the Himalayas is the highest peak above sea level.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A fan-shaped landform built by a river where it meets the sea is called a
questions.explanation: Rivers drop their sediment at the mouth, forming a delta.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A U-shaped valley is typically carved by
questions.explanation: Moving glaciers widen and deepen valleys into a U shape.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are delta regions usually fertile?
options: They are made of bare rock
Rivers deposit fine, nutrient-rich silt there
questions.explanation: Fine alluvium laid down by rivers makes the soil fertile.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Limestone caves with stalactites form mainly because
options: slightly acidic water slowly dissolves limestone
questions.explanation: Chemical weathering by water carrying dissolved carbon dioxide dissolves limestone.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain the difference between weathering and erosion.
questions.answer: Weathering is the breaking down or decay of rock in its place. Erosion is the wearing away of land and the carrying of the material elsewhere by agents such as water, wind and ice.
keyPoints: agents such as water, wind, ice
questions.explanation: Weathering prepares material that erosion then removes.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How are the three main types of rock linked in the rock cycle?
questions.answer: Igneous rock can be broken into sediments that form sedimentary rock, and heat and pressure can change either into metamorphic rock. Any rock may melt to form magma, which cools into new igneous rock.
keyPoints: sedimentary or igneous changed by heat and pressure
questions.explanation: Rocks are continually transformed from one type to another over long periods.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Winds that blow regularly from the east towards the equator in the tropics are called
questions.explanation: Trade winds blow from the subtropical highs towards the equator, from the east.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Gulf Stream is
options: a cold current of the Pacific
a warm ocean current of the North Atlantic
questions.explanation: It carries warm water across the North Atlantic.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Rain caused when moist air is forced to rise over a mountain barrier is called
questions.explanation: Orographic or relief rainfall occurs when air is lifted by mountains.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The windward side of a mountain generally gets more rain than the leeward side because
options: rising moist air cools and condenses on the windward side
the windward side has no clouds
the leeward side is near the sea
questions.explanation: Air loses moisture as it rises, leaving a drier rain shadow beyond the crest.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the natural greenhouse effect important for life on Earth?
options: It cools the Earth to freezing
It traps some heat and keeps the Earth warm enough for life
questions.explanation: Without natural greenhouse gases the average temperature would be far below freezing.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Define weather and climate, and state how they differ.
questions.answer: Weather is the state of the atmosphere at a place over a short time, such as a day. Climate is the average weather of a place over a long period, usually thirty years or more.
questions.explanation: The same place can have varied weather within a stable climate.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain why tropical regions receive more heat than polar regions.
questions.answer: In the tropics the Sun's rays fall almost vertically and are concentrated on a small area. Near the poles they fall at a slant and spread over a larger area and pass through more atmosphere.
questions.explanation: The angle of the Sun's rays determines how intense the heating is.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The soil of the Northern Plains of India is mainly
questions.explanation: Rivers have deposited alluvial soil across the Northern Plains.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Black soil is also known as
questions.explanation: Black soil, regur, is suited to cotton cultivation.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Tropical evergreen forests are found in regions with
questions.explanation: Heat and plentiful rain throughout the year support dense evergreen forests.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In a food chain, which of these is a producer?
questions.explanation: Green plants make their own food and so are producers.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Laterite soil is generally poor in nutrients mainly because
options: heavy rain washes soluble nutrients away
questions.explanation: Intense leaching under heavy rain removes nutrients from the upper soil.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why do desert regions have sparse vegetation of mostly thorny plants?
options: Low rainfall favours plants that reduce water loss
questions.explanation: Thorns and small leaves reduce loss of water in dry conditions.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is conservation of biodiversity, and why is it needed?
questions.answer: Conservation means protecting and wisely using the variety of living things and their habitats. It is needed because species provide food, medicines and raw materials and help keep ecosystems stable.
questions.explanation: Loss of species cannot be reversed and weakens ecosystems.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Describe two ways in which human activities lead to loss of biodiversity.
questions.answer: Clearing forests and draining wetlands for farming, roads or towns destroys habitats. Pollution and excessive hunting or collection of species can also reduce their numbers.
questions.explanation: Habitat loss is among the leading causes of species decline.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these states does the Tropic of Cancer pass through?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer crosses central India, including Madhya Pradesh.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Western Ghats lie along the
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats run parallel to India's west coast.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Ganga is formed at Devprayag by the meeting of the Alaknanda and the
questions.explanation: The Bhagirathi and Alaknanda join at Devprayag to form the Ganga.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these regions of India is particularly earthquake-prone?
questions.explanation: The Himalayan region lies on an active plate boundary.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are the Himalayas and the north-east more earthquake-prone than the interior of the peninsula?
options: They lie near the zone where the Indian plate presses against the Eurasian plate
questions.explanation: Plate collision builds stress in these regions.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Ganga-Brahmaputra delta region often suffers floods mainly because
options: there is no water in the rivers
many rivers carry heavy monsoon flow across low, flat land
it lies on top of mountains
questions.explanation: Heavy monsoon discharge and low relief make flooding frequent.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Give two examples each of east-flowing and west-flowing rivers of peninsular India.
questions.answer: East-flowing rivers include the Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri and Mahanadi. West-flowing rivers include the Narmada and the Tapi.
keyPoints: Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri or Mahanadi flow east
questions.explanation: Most peninsular rivers flow east into the Bay of Bengal, but the Narmada and Tapi flow west.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Suggest two measures to reduce damage from floods.
questions.answer: Building embankments, check dams and reservoirs can control river flow, and planting trees in catchment areas reduces runoff. Early warning systems and avoiding settlement in flood plains also reduce losses.
keyPoints: warning systems and planning of settlements
questions.explanation: Both structural and planning measures reduce flood damage.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Constituent Assembly of India first met in
questions.explanation: Its first meeting took place in December 1946.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Preamble describes India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic
questions.explanation: India is declared a republic, with an elected head of State.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Fundamental Rights are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Part III of the Constitution lists the Fundamental Rights.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Directive Principles of State Policy are in
questions.explanation: Part IV contains the Directive Principles.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Fundamental Rights can be enforced in court, but Directive Principles cannot. What is the role of the Directive Principles?
options: They set goals for governments to work towards for a just society
questions.explanation: They guide State policy even though courts do not enforce them directly.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Providing a special procedure under Article 368 to amend the Constitution shows
options: a balance between flexibility and rigidity
questions.explanation: The Constitution can be amended through a defined procedure, but not by ordinary law-making.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is the Preamble? Mention two ideals it states.
questions.answer: The Preamble is the introductory statement of the Constitution that states its source, aims and values. It speaks of securing justice, liberty, equality and fraternity to all citizens.
questions.explanation: The Preamble summarises the philosophy of the Constitution.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What does it mean to say that the Constitution is the supreme law of the land?
questions.answer: All other laws and government actions must be in accordance with the Constitution. A law that conflicts with it can be declared invalid by the courts, so even the government is bound by it.
keyPoints: conflicting laws can be struck down
questions.explanation: Constitutional supremacy limits the power of the government.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which Article guarantees the Right to Education for children aged 6 to 14 years?
questions.explanation: Article 21A was added by the 86th Amendment.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which Article prohibits the employment of children below 14 in factories and hazardous jobs?
questions.explanation: Article 24 forbids child labour in factories, mines and hazardous work.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Article 25 gives people
options: freedom of conscience and the right to profess, practise and propagate religion
questions.explanation: Article 25 protects freedom of religion, subject to public order, morality and health.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these freedoms is listed in Article 19?
questions.explanation: Article 19 includes speech and expression, assembly, association and movement.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are reasonable restrictions placed on freedom of speech?
options: So that one person's freedom does not harm others or the security of the State
So that only officials may speak
questions.explanation: Rights are exercised within limits so that all can enjoy them.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A person is arrested and not produced before a magistrate within 24 hours. Which Article protects against this?
questions.explanation: Article 22 provides protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In what ways can a person acquire Indian citizenship?
questions.answer: Under the Citizenship Act, 1955, citizenship can be acquired by birth, by descent, by registration and by naturalisation.
questions.explanation: The Act lays down these main modes of acquiring citizenship.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why does the Constitution protect the cultural and educational rights of minorities?
questions.answer: India has many languages, scripts and cultures, and minorities may fear that a larger group could overshadow theirs. The rights let them preserve their culture and run their own educational institutions, which supports equality and diversity.
questions.explanation: Such protection helps ensure that diversity is respected.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who appoints the Prime Minister of India?
questions.explanation: The President appoints the leader who commands majority support in the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The highest court of India is the
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court is the apex court.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Governor is the head of the executive in a
questions.explanation: The Governor is the constitutional head of a State.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The normal term of the Lok Sabha is
questions.explanation: Unless dissolved earlier, the Lok Sabha lasts five years.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the Lok Sabha more powerful than the Rajya Sabha in financial matters?
options: It is chosen by the Rajya Sabha
Money Bills start in the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha can only suggest changes
The Rajya Sabha has no members
questions.explanation: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and its decision on the Bill prevails.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Judicial review means
options: the power of courts to check whether laws and actions follow the Constitution
questions.explanation: Through judicial review, courts can declare laws that violate the Constitution invalid.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is the role of the President in India's parliamentary system?
questions.answer: The President is the constitutional head of State and formally appoints the Prime Minister and other high officials. In practice, the President acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
keyPoints: acts on advice of Council of Ministers
questions.explanation: Real executive power rests with the Council of Ministers.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how checks and balances work among the legislature, executive and judiciary.
questions.answer: The legislature makes laws and questions the executive, the executive implements the laws, and the judiciary can strike down laws or actions that violate the Constitution. Each organ limits the others, so no one acquires unchecked power.
keyPoints: legislature makes laws and questions the executive
questions.explanation: Separation of powers prevents the concentration of authority.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: The idea that people should be treated fairly and receive what is due to them is called
questions.explanation: Justice concerns fairness and giving each person their due.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Which of these is a political right?
questions.explanation: Voting and contesting elections are political rights.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Respecting the dignity of all persons regardless of caste, gender or religion is part of
questions.explanation: Social equality means equal status and dignity for all.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: The book 'On Liberty' was written by
questions.explanation: John Stuart Mill wrote On Liberty in 1859.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Why do many thinkers argue that freedom needs some limits?
options: So that one person's freedom does not harm others
To help rulers stay in power
questions.explanation: Mill's harm principle holds that freedom may be limited to prevent harm to others.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Distributive justice is mainly concerned with
options: how benefits and burdens are fairly shared in society
questions.explanation: It asks how resources, opportunities and responsibilities should be shared.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: What is meant by social justice?
questions.answer: Social justice means fairness in how society treats its members, so that all have equal dignity and a fair chance to meet their basic needs and develop. It involves removing unfair barriers such as discrimination.
questions.explanation: It links equality with the fair sharing of opportunities.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Explain the difference between equality of opportunity and equality of outcome.
questions.answer: Equality of opportunity means everyone gets a fair chance to compete, with no unfair barriers. Equality of outcome means everyone ends up with similar results or rewards. The first allows differences in results because of effort or talent.
questions.explanation: The two ideas answer different questions about fairness.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: India's central bank is the
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: India became independent from British rule in the year
questions.explanation: India became independent on 15 August 1947.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A mixed economy is one that has
options: both a public sector and a private sector
questions.explanation: India adopted a mixed economy with both sectors.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Services such as banking and transport belong to which sector?
questions.explanation: Service activities form the tertiary sector.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A balance of payments crisis in 1991 pushed India to
options: reform and open up the economy
questions.explanation: The crisis led to the 1991 reforms of liberalisation and opening the economy.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why do economists say development usually needs some shift of workers from agriculture to industry and services?
options: Productivity and incomes are generally higher there, and farmland cannot absorb unlimited workers
questions.explanation: Moving to higher-productivity work raises incomes and relieves pressure on land.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is meant by privatisation?
questions.answer: Privatisation means transferring ownership or management of government enterprises to the private sector, or allowing private firms to enter areas earlier reserved for the government.
keyPoints: transfer of ownership or management to private sector
questions.explanation: It reduces the direct role of the State in running businesses.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did India adopt economic planning after independence?
questions.answer: The economy was poor and largely agricultural, with little industry, so the government wanted to use limited resources in an organised way. Planning aimed at growth, self-reliance and reducing poverty and inequality.
questions.explanation: Planning set goals and priorities for development.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A table showing how many times each value occurs is called a
questions.explanation: A frequency distribution lists values with the number of times each occurs.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A circle divided into sectors to show shares of a whole is a
questions.explanation: Each sector of a pie chart represents a share of the total.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The mean of 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 is
questions.explanation: The sum is 150 and 150 divided by 5 is 30.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A histogram is used to display
questions.explanation: A histogram uses adjacent bars for continuous class intervals.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The marks of five students are 40, 45, 50, 55 and 110. Which measure better represents a typical mark?
questions.explanation: The median is 50, while the very high mark pulls the mean up to 60.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A shopkeeper wants to stock the shoe size that is sold most often. Which average should be used?
questions.explanation: The mode is the most frequent value, which is the most sold size.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is an index number? Mention one use.
questions.answer: An index number is a statistical measure that shows the average change in a group of related variables, such as prices, over time compared with a base period. A price index is used to measure inflation.
keyPoints: used for price change or inflation
questions.explanation: Index numbers summarise changes in many items by a single figure.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: When would you use a bar diagram and when a histogram?
questions.answer: A bar diagram shows separate categories or values, with gaps between bars. A histogram shows a frequency distribution of continuous classes, with bars touching, and the area represents frequency.
questions.explanation: The choice depends on whether data are categories or continuous classes.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why was the control of fire important to early humans?
options: It let them make iron tools
It gave warmth, protection and a way to cook food
questions.explanation: Fire provided warmth and light, kept animals away and allowed cooking.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Along which river valley did the early Chinese civilisation develop?
questions.explanation: Early Chinese civilisation arose along the Huang He.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In which ancient Greek city-state did a form of direct democracy develop?
questions.explanation: Athens developed a system in which citizens took part directly in the assembly.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Mehrgarh, an early farming settlement, lies in present-day
questions.explanation: Mehrgarh is in Balochistan, in present-day Pakistan, and shows early farming.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Athenian democracy is often called limited because
options: only adult male citizens could take part, while women, slaves and foreigners were excluded
questions.explanation: Only a minority of residents counted as citizens with political rights.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Cave paintings of animals made by prehistoric people suggest that they
options: observed animals closely and expressed ideas through art
questions.explanation: The paintings show careful observation and the ability to represent ideas visually.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the Bronze Age so called?
questions.answer: It is called the Bronze Age because people in this period learnt to make tools and weapons from bronze, an alloy of copper and tin, which was harder than copper alone.
keyPoints: bronze is an alloy of copper and tin
questions.explanation: The metal gives its name to the period in which it was widely used.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Give one difference between the democracy of ancient Athens and a modern democracy.
questions.answer: In Athens citizens took part directly in the assembly, whereas modern democracies mostly use elected representatives. Also, Athenian citizenship excluded women and slaves, while modern democracies give votes to all adult citizens.
keyPoints: limited citizenship versus universal adult franchise
questions.explanation: Modern democracies are larger and include all adults in political rights.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Constantinople was the capital of which empire?
questions.explanation: Constantinople was the capital of the Eastern Roman or Byzantine Empire.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which city was founded in 762 CE as the capital of the Abbasid caliphs?
questions.explanation: The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur founded Baghdad.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The 'House of Wisdom' in Baghdad was a centre of
questions.explanation: Scholars there translated and studied works from many languages.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Magna Carta of 1215 limited the powers of the king of
questions.explanation: English barons forced King John to accept the Magna Carta.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the Magna Carta important in the long run?
options: It gave every person the vote
It supported the idea that even a ruler is bound by law
questions.explanation: It became a symbol of limits on royal power and of the rule of law.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The phrase 'Pax Mongolica' is used for a period of
options: relatively safe travel and trade across much of Eurasia
questions.explanation: Mongol rule over a vast area made long-distance travel safer for a time.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why was Constantinople an important city?
questions.answer: It was the capital of the Eastern Roman or Byzantine Empire and lay at a crossroads between Europe and Asia, making it a rich centre of trade. It was captured by the Ottomans in 1453.
keyPoints: trade crossroads between Europe and Asia
questions.explanation: Its location gave it both commercial and strategic importance.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how scholars writing in Arabic helped preserve and develop knowledge in the medieval period.
questions.answer: Scholars translated Greek and Indian works into Arabic, which kept them from being lost. They also added their own advances in mathematics, medicine and astronomy, and this knowledge later reached Europe.
questions.explanation: Learning in the Islamic world was a link between ancient and later knowledge.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen of 1789 was issued in
questions.explanation: The National Assembly of France issued the Declaration in 1789.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which scientist is known for the laws of motion and the theory of universal gravitation?
questions.explanation: Isaac Newton formulated the laws of motion and gravitation.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The storming of the Bastille on 14 July 1789 is a symbol of
questions.explanation: The attack on the Bastille prison marked the start of the French Revolution.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Communist Manifesto, by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, was published in
questions.explanation: The Manifesto appeared in 1848.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did financial trouble contribute to the outbreak of the French Revolution?
options: The state had a surplus of money
The state was in debt and taxes fell heavily on the common people, creating discontent
There were no taxes in France
questions.explanation: Debt and unfair taxation increased anger among the Third Estate.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did the Third Estate, although the largest group in France, have little power before 1789?
options: Voting in the Estates-General was by order, so it could be outvoted by the two privileged orders
The king was elected by it
questions.explanation: Each estate had one vote, so the clergy and nobility could outvote the commoners.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: State two causes of the American War of Independence.
questions.answer: The British Parliament imposed taxes on the thirteen colonies, which had no representatives in it, and colonists objected to 'taxation without representation'. They also resented British control over their trade and political life.
questions.explanation: Disputes over taxation and self-rule led to war and independence.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how the Industrial Revolution brought both benefits and hardships to workers.
questions.answer: Factory jobs offered wages and cheaper goods became available. However, many workers, including children, faced long hours, low pay, unsafe conditions and crowded, unhealthy housing in towns.
questions.explanation: Early industrial growth changed living standards unevenly.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Himalayas lie in which continent?
questions.explanation: The Himalayas stretch across South Asia.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which is the largest continent in area?
questions.explanation: Asia is the largest continent.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The idea that the continents have moved over time is known as
questions.explanation: Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift in the early twentieth century.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Wegener proposed that all continents were once joined in a single landmass called
questions.explanation: Pangaea means 'all land'.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The matching coastlines of Africa and South America and the similar fossils found on both support the idea that
options: these continents were once joined together
questions.explanation: These are key pieces of evidence for continental drift.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Fold mountains such as the Himalayas form mainly where
options: two plates collide and compress sediments
questions.explanation: Collision of plates squeezes and uplifts rock layers into folds.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is an earthquake? Define the focus and the epicentre.
questions.answer: An earthquake is a sudden shaking of the ground caused by the release of energy in the Earth's crust. The focus is the point inside the Earth where the rupture begins and the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above it.
keyPoints: focus is the point of origin below ground
epicentre is the point directly above
questions.explanation: The epicentre usually experiences the strongest shaking.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how a volcanic eruption can create new landforms as well as hazards.
questions.answer: Lava and ash that cool and pile up can build volcanic cones, plateaus and islands, and weathered volcanic material can form fertile soil. At the same time, eruptions can destroy settlements, crops and lives through lava, ash and gases.
keyPoints: lava and ash build cones, plateaus, islands
questions.explanation: Eruptions both build land and cause disasters.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure rainfall?
questions.explanation: A rain gauge collects and measures rainfall.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The imaginary line at 0 degrees latitude is called the
questions.explanation: The Equator is the 0 degree line of latitude.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these is a cold ocean current?
questions.explanation: The Peru Current carries cold water northward along the west coast of South America.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Ocean tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of
questions.explanation: The Moon, and to a lesser degree the Sun, pull on the oceans, producing tides.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Spring tides, the highest high tides, occur when
options: the Moon is at its first quarter
the Sun, Earth and Moon are in a line at new moon and full moon
questions.explanation: When the Sun and Moon pull in the same line, their effects add up.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are temperatures high throughout the year near the equator?
options: The Sun's rays are nearly overhead all through the year
questions.explanation: Nearly vertical rays give strong heating in all months.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What causes winds to blow?
questions.answer: Unequal heating of the Earth's surface creates differences in air pressure, and air moves from high-pressure areas to low-pressure areas as wind. The rotation of the Earth deflects the direction of the winds.
keyPoints: air moves from high to low pressure
questions.explanation: Pressure differences set the air in motion.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how the monsoon is related to the differential heating of land and sea.
questions.answer: In summer the land heats faster than the sea, so a low-pressure area forms over the land and cooler, moist air from the sea blows in, bringing rain. In winter the land cools faster, so the winds reverse and blow from land to sea.
keyPoints: land heats faster than sea in summer
low pressure draws moist winds from sea
questions.explanation: Seasonal reversal of winds is the basis of the monsoon.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these is a renewable resource?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is continually available and does not get used up.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Plants release oxygen during
questions.explanation: Oxygen is released as a by-product of photosynthesis.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The washing down of soluble nutrients from the upper soil by water is called
questions.explanation: Leaching removes dissolved minerals from the topsoil.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these is a method of soil conservation on slopes?
questions.explanation: Terraces slow down runoff and reduce erosion on slopes.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Contour ploughing helps conserve soil because
options: furrows along the slope slow the flow of water
questions.explanation: Ploughing across the slope creates barriers to downhill flow of water.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why can a foreign species introduced into a new habitat sometimes cause harm?
options: It may out-compete native species that have no natural check on it
questions.explanation: Without natural predators, an introduced species can spread and displace native ones.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What are a food chain and a food web?
questions.answer: A food chain shows a single sequence of who eats whom, beginning with a producer. A food web is a network of many interconnected food chains in an ecosystem.
keyPoints: food chain is a single sequence
questions.explanation: Food webs show the complex feeding relationships in an ecosystem.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are wetlands considered important ecosystems?
questions.answer: Wetlands act like sponges that absorb floodwater and release it slowly. They also filter pollutants from water and provide habitats for many birds, fish and plants.
questions.explanation: Wetlands support biodiversity and protect against floods.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal and which ocean wash the coast of peninsular India?
questions.explanation: The peninsula juts into the Indian Ocean.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Thar Desert lies mainly in which state?
questions.explanation: Most of the Thar Desert is in Rajasthan.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Brahmaputra is known by what name in Tibet?
questions.explanation: In Tibet the river is called the Tsangpo.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Winter rainfall in north-western India is brought mainly by
options: tropical cyclones of the Bay of Bengal
questions.explanation: Western disturbances from the Mediterranean region bring winter rain to the north-west.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why does the Tamil Nadu coast receive much of its rain in October to December?
options: The southwest monsoon is strongest then
The retreating north-east monsoon picks up moisture from the Bay of Bengal
questions.explanation: Retreating monsoon winds blowing over the Bay of Bengal bring rain to the south-east coast.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The interior of the Deccan Plateau is relatively dry because
options: it lies far from any hills
it lies in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats
questions.explanation: Moist winds lose most of their water on the windward Ghats.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name the four seasons recognised in the Indian climate.
questions.answer: Winter (cold weather season), summer (hot weather season), the southwest monsoon season and the season of the retreating monsoon.
questions.explanation: The Indian year is commonly divided into these four seasons.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Describe the importance of the Himalayas to India.
questions.answer: The Himalayas act as a climatic barrier, blocking cold northern winds and helping to bring monsoon rain. They are the source of major perennial rivers, hold forests and minerals, and form a natural defensive barrier.
questions.explanation: The mountains influence climate, water and security.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly was moved by
questions.explanation: Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution in December 1946.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Constitution of India is
questions.explanation: India has a written Constitution adopted by the Constituent Assembly.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 added Fundamental Duties.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The division of powers between the Union and the States is listed in the
questions.explanation: The Seventh Schedule has the Union, State and Concurrent Lists.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A subject in the Concurrent List means that
options: only the Centre can make laws on it
only the States can make laws on it
no one can make laws on it
both Parliament and State legislatures may make laws, with the Union law prevailing in a conflict
questions.explanation: On Concurrent subjects both levels can legislate, but Parliament's law prevails if they conflict.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Adopting universal adult franchise at the start, despite widespread illiteracy, showed
options: a commitment to political equality for all citizens
questions.explanation: Every adult was given an equal vote regardless of education or property.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name the three lists in the Seventh Schedule and give one subject for each.
questions.answer: The Union List, with subjects such as defence; the State List, with subjects such as police; and the Concurrent List, with subjects such as education.
questions.explanation: The three lists distribute legislative powers in the federal system.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why do federal countries divide powers between the central and State governments?
questions.answer: In a large and diverse country, local governments can deal better with local needs, while a central government handles national matters such as defence. Dividing power also prevents too much concentration of authority.
questions.explanation: Federalism combines unity with regional self-rule.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Article 23 prohibits
options: traffic in human beings and forced labour
questions.explanation: Article 23 bans human trafficking and forced labour.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The minimum voting age for Indian citizens is
questions.explanation: The voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 by the 61st Amendment.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which writ commands a public official to perform a duty that he or she has failed to carry out?
questions.explanation: Mandamus means 'we command'.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Fundamental Duties of citizens are listed in
questions.explanation: Article 51A lists the Fundamental Duties.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the Right against Exploitation especially important for weaker sections of society?
options: It lets them avoid all laws
It protects against forced labour, trafficking and child labour, which mostly harm the poor and powerless
questions.explanation: The poor and powerless are the most likely victims of exploitation.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Constitution allows special provisions for women, children and disadvantaged groups. This shows that equality in the Constitution means
options: equal treatment of equals along with positive steps for the disadvantaged
questions.explanation: Real equality may need special measures to remove disadvantages.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What are Fundamental Duties? Name any two.
questions.answer: Fundamental Duties are the moral obligations of citizens listed in Article 51A. Examples include respecting the Constitution, the national flag and anthem, protecting the environment and safeguarding public property.
questions.explanation: Duties remind citizens of their responsibilities to the nation and society.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the Right to Equality important for a democracy? Give two points.
questions.answer: A democracy treats every citizen as having equal worth, so laws must apply equally and no one should face discrimination on grounds such as religion, caste, sex or place of birth. Equal access to public places and jobs allows all to take part in public life.
questions.explanation: Without equality, democratic participation would be unfair.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Rajya Sabha is presided over by the
questions.explanation: The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The head of the government at the Centre is the
