questions.explanation: The Prime Minister heads the Council of Ministers and the government.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The President of India is elected by
options: an electoral college of elected members of Parliament and State legislatures
questions.explanation: The election is indirect, through an electoral college.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Question Hour in Parliament is meant for
questions.explanation: During Question Hour members question ministers on their work.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is Question Hour useful for democratic accountability?
options: It lets ministers give orders to members
It allows elected members to question the government and require answers about its work
questions.explanation: Questions make the executive explain and justify its actions to the legislature.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A law passed by Parliament is challenged as violating the Fundamental Rights. Which body decides if it is valid?
options: The Supreme Court, through judicial review
questions.explanation: Courts can strike down laws that violate the Constitution.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What are the functions of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
questions.answer: The Speaker presides over the sittings, maintains order and discipline, decides on points of procedure and allows members to speak. The Speaker is expected to be impartial.
questions.explanation: The Speaker ensures orderly conduct of business.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Describe how an ordinary bill becomes an Act in Parliament.
questions.answer: A bill is introduced in a House, discussed and voted on, and then sent to the other House for the same process. After both Houses pass it, it goes to the President, whose assent turns it into an Act.
keyPoints: introduction and discussion in a House
questions.explanation: A bill needs the approval of both Houses and the President to become law.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Which of these is an example of a civil liberty?
questions.explanation: Freedom of speech protects individuals from interference by the State.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Which concept refers to the supreme authority of a State over its territory?
questions.explanation: Sovereignty means final authority within the territory of the State.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Economic equality is concerned with
options: reducing large gaps in wealth and income between people
questions.explanation: It deals with the distribution of wealth and income.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Affirmative action refers to
options: policies to help disadvantaged groups improve their opportunities
questions.explanation: These are measures intended to correct unequal opportunities.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: A government provides free schooling to children from poor families. Which value does this most directly promote?
questions.explanation: Free schooling gives disadvantaged children a fairer chance.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Why might a society that gives only legal equality still be unjust?
options: Because social and economic disadvantages can stop people from using their equal rights
Because all people are the same
questions.explanation: Equal rights on paper may not help those lacking resources or opportunity.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: What is meant by the 'harm principle'?
questions.answer: The harm principle, associated with J. S. Mill, holds that a person's freedom may be limited only to prevent harm to others, and not merely because others dislike what the person does.
keyPoints: freedom limited to prevent harm to others
questions.explanation: It is a standard test for justified limits on liberty.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: How can freedom and equality sometimes pull in different directions? Give an example.
questions.answer: Complete freedom in the market can let some people become far richer than others, creating inequality. Taxing the rich to help the poor promotes equality but limits the freedom of the rich to use all their income.
questions.explanation: Societies balance the two values through laws and policies.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Planning Commission of India was set up in the year
questions.explanation: The Planning Commission was set up in March 1950.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Farming, fishing and mining belong to which sector?
questions.explanation: Activities that use natural resources directly form the primary sector.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In which year were 14 major commercial banks nationalised in India?
questions.explanation: Fourteen major banks were nationalised in 1969.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures
options: the total value of final goods and services produced within a country in a year
questions.explanation: GDP is the value of final output produced within a country in a period.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why can high inflation hurt poor households the most?
options: Their incomes are low or fixed, so rising prices reduce what they can buy
questions.explanation: Low and fixed incomes buy less when prices rise, and the poor spend most income on necessities.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why does a country with low savings find it hard to finance investment?
options: Investment funds come largely from savings
questions.explanation: Domestic savings are the main source of funds for investment.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Distinguish between the public sector and the private sector.
questions.answer: The public sector consists of enterprises owned and run by the government, such as railways. The private sector consists of businesses owned by individuals or companies, mainly to earn profit.
keyPoints: private sector owned by individuals or companies
questions.explanation: A mixed economy has both sectors.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: State two reasons why unemployment can persist in a developing economy like India.
questions.answer: Many people are engaged in agriculture, where more workers are present than the land needs, which causes disguised unemployment, and the work is seasonal. Industry and services may not grow fast enough to absorb the growing workforce.
keyPoints: disguised or seasonal unemployment in agriculture
questions.explanation: Structural features of the economy limit job creation.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The difference between the largest and the smallest values in a data set is called the
questions.explanation: Range equals the maximum value minus the minimum value.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Data collected over successive years are called a
questions.explanation: Data arranged by time are called a time series.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The median of 4, 8, 6 and 10 is
questions.explanation: Arranged as 4, 6, 8, 10, the median is the average of 6 and 8, which is 7.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In a frequency table, the number of times a value occurs is called its
questions.explanation: Frequency means the count of occurrences.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The mean of five numbers is 12. If a sixth number, 18, is added, the new mean is
questions.explanation: The old total is 60; adding 18 gives 78, and 78 divided by 6 is 13.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A survey asked only people leaving a luxury shopping mall about their spending. Why might it misrepresent the whole city?
options: The sample is not representative of the city's population
questions.explanation: A biased sample does not reflect the whole population.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: State two advantages of presenting data in diagrams.
questions.answer: Diagrams make data easier to understand at a glance and help in comparing values. They are also attractive and easy to remember.
questions.explanation: Visual presentation makes patterns clearer than raw numbers.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the arithmetic mean affected by extreme values? Illustrate with an example.
questions.answer: The mean uses every value, so a very large or very small one shifts it. For 10, 12, 14, 16 and 100 the mean is 30.4 although most values are near 10 to 16, whereas the median is 14.
keyPoints: example with a comparison to the median
questions.explanation: This is why the median may describe skewed data better.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Hammurabi, known for a famous code of laws, was a king of
questions.explanation: Hammurabi ruled Babylon in Mesopotamia.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The early use of the wheel and of cuneiform writing is associated with which civilisation?
questions.explanation: The Sumerians of southern Mesopotamia developed cuneiform and used wheeled vehicles early.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Cuneiform signs were made by pressing a reed stylus into
questions.explanation: Mesopotamian scribes wrote on wet clay tablets.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did ancient Egyptians practise mummification?
options: They believed in life after death and wanted to preserve the body
It was a way of making cloth
questions.explanation: Preserving the body was linked to beliefs about the afterlife.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A ruler's laws carved on a stone pillar and displayed for people to see suggest that
options: the ruler tried to apply written, publicly known laws across the kingdom
questions.explanation: Publicly displayed laws point to an attempt at uniform, known rules.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did Sumerian city-states need record keeping?
options: Managing grain stores, trade and taxes required accurate records, which encouraged writing
questions.explanation: The needs of administration and trade helped writing to develop.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What were ziggurats?
questions.answer: Ziggurats were large stepped temple towers built in Mesopotamian cities, dedicated to the city's god. They were also centres of religious and economic life.
questions.explanation: They show the importance of religion in early city life.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how the use of iron changed farming and warfare.
questions.answer: Iron was harder and cheaper than bronze, so iron ploughs and tools made it easier to clear land and increase crop production. Iron weapons were stronger and more widely available, which changed warfare.
keyPoints: better ploughs and tools raised production
questions.explanation: Iron technology spread widely because ore was more common than the metals for bronze.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Ottoman Turks captured Constantinople in the year
questions.explanation: Constantinople fell to the Ottomans in 1453.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: William of Normandy won the Battle of Hastings in the year
questions.explanation: The Norman conquest of England began with Hastings in 1066.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Charlemagne was crowned Emperor in 800 CE by the
questions.explanation: Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne in Rome.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In medieval Europe, knights were
options: mounted warriors who served a lord
questions.explanation: Knights fought on horseback in return for land or protection.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Monasteries in medieval Europe helped to preserve learning because
questions.explanation: Before printing, monks copied and kept many ancient and religious texts.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Black Death of the fourteenth century affected European feudal society because
options: the death of many workers made labour scarce and gave peasants more bargaining power
it ended all trade for ever
questions.explanation: With fewer workers, labourers could demand better terms.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Describe the role of the Church in medieval Europe.
questions.answer: The Church was the main religious authority and also owned land and ran schools and monasteries. It influenced the lives of people and the decisions of rulers.
keyPoints: owned land, ran schools and monasteries
questions.explanation: The Church was one of the most powerful institutions of the period.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Compare the Roman Republic and the Roman Empire in two respects.
questions.answer: In the Republic, power was shared among elected magistrates and the Senate, while in the Empire the emperor held supreme power. The Republic was mainly centred on the city and its neighbourhood, whereas the Empire ruled a far larger territory.
questions.explanation: The Republic gave way to rule by an emperor from the time of Augustus.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which English scientist is associated with the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin proposed evolution by natural selection.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Renaissance in Europe is generally dated to roughly which period?
questions.explanation: The Renaissance began in the fourteenth century in Italy and spread over the next centuries.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in Rome?
questions.explanation: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling in the early sixteenth century.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The 'spinning jenny' was invented to speed up the making of
questions.explanation: The spinning jenny allowed several threads to be spun at once.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Reformation weakened the religious unity of Western Europe because
options: new Protestant churches broke away from the Pope's authority
questions.explanation: Protestant churches formed independently of Rome, ending the single Western Church.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which was a long-term effect of the American and French Revolutions?
options: They ended all monarchies at once
They stopped the growth of nationalism
They spread ideas of popular sovereignty and rights that inspired later movements
questions.explanation: Their ideas influenced reform and independence movements in many places.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is meant by humanism in the Renaissance?
questions.answer: Humanism was an outlook that gave importance to human beings, their abilities and worldly life, and encouraged the study of classical Greek and Roman writings. It led to new interest in art, literature and science.
keyPoints: importance of human beings and worldly life
new interest in arts and sciences
questions.explanation: It was the central intellectual movement of the Renaissance.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how the Scientific Revolution changed the way people understood the world.
questions.answer: Thinkers such as Copernicus, Galileo and Newton relied on observation, experiment and mathematics rather than only on old authorities. They showed that nature follows laws which can be discovered, which changed ideas about the universe.
questions.explanation: It established the scientific method as a way of gaining knowledge.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these is a sedimentary rock?
questions.explanation: Sandstone forms from compacted sand grains.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A mountain through which lava erupts is called a
questions.explanation: A volcano is an opening through which lava, ash and gases are ejected.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The 'Ring of Fire' around the Pacific Ocean is known for
questions.explanation: Many plate boundaries around the Pacific cause many earthquakes and volcanoes.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A flat-topped, elevated area of land is called a
questions.explanation: A plateau is raised land with a relatively flat top.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Mid-ocean ridges form where plates
options: move apart and new crust forms from rising magma
questions.explanation: At diverging boundaries magma rises and creates new oceanic crust.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are deep ocean trenches found near zones where plates converge?
options: One plate sinks beneath another, creating a deep trench
questions.explanation: Subduction pulls the sinking plate down, forming a trench.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name any two types of mountains and give an example of each.
questions.answer: Fold mountains, such as the Himalayas or the Alps, are formed by compression of rock layers. Volcanic mountains, such as Mount Fuji, are built by erupted lava and ash.
questions.explanation: Mountains are classified by the way they were formed.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Describe how the work of a river changes from its upper course to its lower course.
questions.answer: In the upper course the river flows fast on steep slopes and mainly erodes, cutting deep V-shaped valleys. In the lower course the slope is gentle and the river deposits sediments, forming floodplains and deltas.
questions.explanation: Slope and speed of flow determine whether a river erodes or deposits.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Earth completes one rotation on its axis in about
questions.explanation: One rotation takes about 24 hours and causes day and night.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which gas in the air is used by living beings for breathing?
questions.explanation: Most organisms need oxygen for respiration.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Because of the Earth's rotation, winds in the Northern Hemisphere are deflected to the
questions.explanation: The Coriolis effect turns winds to the right in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The imaginary lines that run from the North Pole to the South Pole are called
questions.explanation: Lines of longitude, or meridians, join the poles.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: On which date does the Sun shine vertically over the Tropic of Cancer?
questions.explanation: The Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer at the June solstice.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why do hot deserts often show a large difference between day and night temperatures?
options: Clear, dry air lets heat escape quickly after sunset
questions.explanation: With little cloud or moisture, the ground loses heat rapidly at night.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Differentiate between evaporation and condensation.
questions.answer: Evaporation is the change of liquid water into water vapour, usually by heat. Condensation is the change of water vapour back into liquid droplets when air cools.
questions.explanation: Both are steps of the water cycle.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how burning fossil fuels can strengthen the greenhouse effect.
questions.answer: Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas. More greenhouse gases in the air trap more heat, which can raise the average temperature of the Earth.
questions.explanation: Rising greenhouse gas levels intensify the natural greenhouse effect.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these is a fossil fuel?
questions.explanation: Coal formed from the remains of ancient plants.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A habitat is
options: the natural home of an organism
questions.explanation: A habitat is where an organism normally lives.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which kind of forest sheds its leaves in the dry season?
questions.explanation: Monsoon forests shed leaves in the dry season to reduce water loss.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Tundra vegetation consists mainly of
questions.explanation: The cold polar climate supports only mosses, lichens and small plants.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Planting trees on bare land helps by
options: absorbing carbon dioxide, binding soil and providing habitat
questions.explanation: Trees take in carbon dioxide, hold the soil and shelter animals.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Coral reefs are sometimes called the rainforests of the sea because they
options: support a very large variety of marine life
questions.explanation: Reefs shelter a great diversity of species, like rainforests on land.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is a biosphere reserve?
questions.answer: A biosphere reserve is a protected area set aside to conserve the plants, animals and microbes of an ecosystem along with the traditional ways of life of people living there.
questions.explanation: Biosphere reserves aim to protect nature while allowing sustainable use.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Soil is renewable but forms very slowly. What does this imply for its use?
questions.answer: Soil takes hundreds or thousands of years to form, so soil lost by erosion cannot be quickly replaced. It must be protected by measures such as terracing, afforestation and avoiding overgrazing.
questions.explanation: Slow formation makes careful use of soil essential.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Peninsular India is bordered on the east by the
questions.explanation: The Bay of Bengal lies along the east coast.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Standard Meridian of India is approximately at
questions.explanation: Indian Standard Time is based on 82°30′ E.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie in the
questions.explanation: These islands lie in the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Lakshadweep Islands are mostly
questions.explanation: The Lakshadweep group consists of coral atolls.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Indo-Gangetic plains support a dense population mainly because
options: fertile soil, water and flat land favour agriculture and settlement
questions.explanation: Fertile alluvium, rivers and level land support intensive farming and large populations.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Western Ghats' windward slopes have dense evergreen forests because
options: the southwest monsoon causes heavy orographic rain
questions.explanation: Moist monsoon winds are forced up the slopes, giving heavy rainfall.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name any four major soil types found in India.
questions.answer: Alluvial soil, black soil, red soil, laterite soil and desert (arid) soil are among the major types.
questions.explanation: Soil types in India are related to rock, climate and relief.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the climate of India described as monsoon type even though there are large regional variations?
questions.answer: The seasonal reversal of winds and the arrival of the southwest monsoon rain shape the rhythm of the year across most of the country. Regional differences in temperature and rainfall occur within this common pattern.
keyPoints: monsoon rain dominates the annual cycle
questions.explanation: The monsoon is the unifying element of Indian climate.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India on
questions.explanation: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: India is described as a 'Union of States' in which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 1 says that India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these is a Directive Principle of State Policy?
options: Equal pay for equal work for men and women
questions.explanation: Equal pay for equal work is a Directive Principle.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Constitution of India provides for
options: single citizenship for the whole country
questions.explanation: India has a single citizenship common to the whole country.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Constitution divides powers between the Union and States but gives the Centre special strength in some situations. This arrangement is best described as
options: a federation with a strong Centre
questions.explanation: India is a federal system with a tilt towards the Centre.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did the framers make the Fundamental Rights enforceable by courts?
options: So that rights stay as advice only
So that rights are protected even against encroachment by the government
To reduce the role of courts
questions.explanation: Court enforcement gives citizens a remedy against violations, including by the State.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What was the Constituent Assembly of India and what task did it perform?
questions.answer: The Constituent Assembly was a body of representatives that met from 1946 to draft the Constitution of India. It debated and adopted the Constitution in 1949.
questions.explanation: The Assembly's work produced the Constitution that came into force in 1950.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is meant by the 'basic structure' of the Constitution?
questions.answer: The Supreme Court held in the Kesavananda Bharati case of 1973 that Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot alter its basic structure. Features such as democracy and judicial review are seen as part of it.
questions.explanation: The doctrine limits Parliament's power to amend the Constitution.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of
options: religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth
questions.explanation: Article 15 forbids discrimination on those grounds.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which Article guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment?
questions.explanation: Article 16 deals with equality of opportunity in public employment.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which writ is issued to stop a lower court from acting beyond its jurisdiction?
questions.explanation: A writ of prohibition forbids a lower court from exceeding its authority.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Under which Article can High Courts issue writs?
questions.explanation: Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A student says her right to freedom of expression allows her to abuse a classmate in public. What is the correct response?
options: Freedom of expression is subject to reasonable restrictions and does not allow harming others' dignity
questions.explanation: Rights come with reasonable limits so that others' rights are protected.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the Right to Information considered useful in a democracy?
options: It helps citizens hold public authorities accountable
questions.explanation: Access to information lets citizens check the work of public bodies.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: State two differences between the rights of a citizen and those of a foreigner in India.
questions.answer: Citizens can vote and contest elections and hold some high public offices, which foreigners cannot. Some Fundamental Rights, such as those in Articles 15, 16 and 19, are available only to citizens, while rights such as Article 21 are available to all persons.
keyPoints: citizens can vote and hold certain offices
some Fundamental Rights only for citizens
questions.explanation: Citizenship carries additional political rights.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How does the idea of secularism help in a society with many religions?
questions.answer: A secular State does not favour any religion, so followers of all faiths have equal rights and can practise their beliefs freely. This helps maintain peace and equal citizenship in a diverse society.
keyPoints: State does not favour any religion
equal rights and freedom to practise
questions.explanation: Secularism protects both religious freedom and equality.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who heads the real executive in a State government?
questions.explanation: The Chief Minister, with the State Council of Ministers, exercises real executive power.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Elections to the Lok Sabha are held on the basis of
questions.explanation: Every adult citizen has one vote under universal adult franchise.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Judges of the Supreme Court are formally appointed by the
questions.explanation: The President appoints them after consultation, as laid down by the Constitution.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A no-confidence motion tests whether the government
options: still has the support of the majority in the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: If the motion is passed, the government must resign.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is it important to keep the judiciary separate from the executive?
options: Judges can decide cases impartially without pressure from the government
Ministers should choose judges at will
questions.explanation: Independence allows courts to give fair judgments, even against the government.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why does India's Parliament have two Houses?
options: To represent the people directly and also the States, allowing review of legislation
questions.explanation: The Lok Sabha represents the people and the Rajya Sabha represents the States, and it provides a second review of laws.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Mention two functions of the Chief Minister of a State.
questions.answer: The Chief Minister heads the State Council of Ministers and leads the State government's policy. The Chief Minister also advises the Governor and allocates portfolios among ministers.
questions.explanation: The Chief Minister is the real head of the State executive.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is Public Interest Litigation (PIL), and why is it useful?
questions.answer: PIL allows any person or group to approach a court for the protection of the public interest or the rights of people who cannot easily approach it themselves. It makes justice more accessible to the poor and disadvantaged.
keyPoints: anyone may approach court on public issues
helps those who cannot approach court
questions.explanation: PIL widened the role of courts in protecting public interests.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Who wrote the book 'The Social Contract'?
questions.explanation: Rousseau wrote The Social Contract in 1762.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Treating everyone alike under the law, with no special privileges, is called
questions.explanation: Equality before law means that the law applies equally to all.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: A right that belongs to every person simply because they are human is called a
questions.explanation: Human rights belong to all persons by virtue of being human.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: In politics, the word 'minority' usually refers to a group that is
options: smaller in number than the rest of the population and often with a distinct identity
questions.explanation: Minorities are groups that are fewer in number than the rest and often share a distinct identity.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Why is the rule of law essential for protecting liberty?
options: It lets rulers act as they please
It ensures those in power are also bound by law and cannot act arbitrarily
It allows laws to change daily
questions.explanation: When even rulers must follow the law, citizens are secure against arbitrary action.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Which situation best shows a lack of procedural justice?
options: Both sides are heard before a decision
A person is punished without being allowed to present their side
questions.explanation: Fair procedure requires a hearing for the person affected.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Name and briefly explain the main kinds of equality.
questions.answer: Political equality gives all citizens equal rights such as the vote. Social equality means equal status and dignity, without discrimination. Economic equality concerns reducing large gaps in wealth and income.
questions.explanation: Different kinds of equality relate to politics, society and the economy.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Why does a fair procedure matter for justice?
questions.answer: Even a correct outcome may seem unjust if the process was biased or secret. A fair hearing, equal treatment and reasons for decisions build trust and reduce the chance of error or abuse.
questions.explanation: Justice depends on how decisions are reached as well as on the results.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which type of economic system did India adopt after independence?
questions.explanation: India adopted a mixed economy with public and private sectors.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Green Revolution began in India in the
questions.explanation: High-yielding varieties were introduced in the mid-to-late 1960s.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In economics, 'globalisation' refers to
options: greater integration of economies through trade, investment and technology flows
questions.explanation: Globalisation means growing linkages among national economies.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The World Trade Organisation (WTO) was established in the year
questions.explanation: The WTO was set up in 1995.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why was agriculture given priority in the First Five Year Plan?
options: Because of food shortages after independence and the need to raise output
questions.explanation: The economy was largely agricultural and food supply was a pressing concern.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Opening the economy to imports can affect a domestic producer by
options: bringing greater competition, which may push for improvement or cause losses
questions.explanation: Competition from imports can raise efficiency but hurt weak firms.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is meant by the poverty line?
questions.answer: The poverty line is a minimum level of income or consumption expenditure, set to buy a basic standard of food and other necessities. People below it are counted as poor.
keyPoints: minimum level of income or expenditure
questions.explanation: It is used to measure the extent of poverty.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain why the Green Revolution had unequal regional effects.
questions.answer: It worked best in areas with assured irrigation and good infrastructure, such as Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, and mainly for wheat and rice. Regions without irrigation and farmers with small holdings gained less.
keyPoints: less gain for unirrigated areas and small farmers
questions.explanation: The new technology needed water, inputs and credit.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A study that collects information from every household in a village uses the method of
questions.explanation: Covering every unit of the population is a census.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A questionnaire is a tool used for
questions.explanation: A questionnaire is a set of questions for collecting data.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The arithmetic mean of 2, 3, 3, 4 and 8 is
questions.explanation: The sum is 20, and 20 divided by 5 is 4.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The mode of the data 2, 3, 3, 4 and 8 is
questions.explanation: The value 3 occurs most often.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A price index in the base year is 100. If the index this year is 125, prices have
options: risen by 25 per cent compared with the base year
questions.explanation: An index of 125 means a 25 per cent rise over the base year.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In a country where a few people are extremely rich, the mean income may
options: be lower than what most people earn
overstate what a typical person earns
questions.explanation: A few very high incomes pull the mean above the typical income.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is the difference between a population and a sample?
questions.answer: A population is the entire group about which information is wanted. A sample is a smaller part of that group chosen to represent it.
questions.explanation: Samples are used to learn about a population without studying every unit.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why should a researcher be careful when using secondary data?
questions.answer: Secondary data were collected by others for a different purpose, so definitions may differ, they may be outdated or contain errors. The researcher should check the source and its reliability.
questions.explanation: Data quality affects the reliability of conclusions.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The rulers of ancient Egypt were called
questions.explanation: Egyptian kings were known as pharaohs.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Indus Valley civilisation developed mainly in the north-western part of which region?
questions.explanation: Its sites lie in the north-west of the Indian subcontinent.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Lothal, a Harappan site, is known for its
questions.explanation: A structure at Lothal is widely regarded as a dockyard.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which crops were grown by the Harappans?
questions.explanation: Wheat and barley were among the main Harappan crops.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Harappan-style seals have been found in Mesopotamia. This indicates
options: there was no contact between regions
that Mesopotamia ruled the Indus region
trade or contact between the two regions
questions.explanation: Objects from one region found in another point to contact and exchange.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A farming village begins to produce more grain than it needs. What is the most likely long-term result?
options: Some people take up other occupations and trade develops
questions.explanation: Surplus allows specialisation and exchange.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Mention three features of an early urban civilisation.
questions.answer: Early urban civilisations had cities with large populations, a surplus of food and specialised occupations. They usually had some form of government, trade, and often writing.
questions.explanation: These features distinguish cities from simple villages.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How do archaeologists reconstruct the past from material remains? Give an example.
questions.answer: They excavate and study objects such as tools, pottery, ruins and bones, and compare them to work out how people lived, what they ate and how they traded. For example, grain remains show which crops were grown.
keyPoints: study tools, pottery, ruins and bones
questions.explanation: Material evidence is the main source where there are no written records.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which city is the birthplace of Prophet Muhammad and is holy to Muslims?
questions.explanation: Mecca is the birthplace of the Prophet and the site of the Kaaba.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Silk Road connected China with
questions.explanation: The Silk Road linked China to Central Asia and the Mediterranean.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Roman Republic was governed mainly by
questions.explanation: Elected officials and the Senate ran the Republic.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Gladiators in ancient Rome fought in large arenas such as the
questions.explanation: The Colosseum in Rome hosted gladiatorial contests.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which is a lasting effect of Roman rule in Europe?
options: Languages such as Italian, French and Spanish developed from Latin
questions.explanation: The Romance languages grew out of the Latin spoken in the empire.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did the early spread of Islamic rule help link Asia, Africa and Europe?
options: A large area shared a common language of learning and trade routes, which aided exchange
questions.explanation: A wide area under related rule made travel and exchange of goods and ideas easier.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What were the Crusades?
questions.answer: The Crusades were a series of military expeditions between the eleventh and thirteenth centuries, launched by European Christian rulers and the Pope, mainly to gain control of Jerusalem and the Holy Land from Muslim rulers.
keyPoints: aimed at control of Jerusalem and the Holy Land
questions.explanation: They affected relations and trade between Europe and the Middle East.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain why the Western Roman Empire is said to have fallen because of both internal weakness and outside pressure.
questions.answer: Internally, it faced political instability, economic difficulties and the high cost of defending its borders. Externally, groups such as the Germanic peoples attacked and settled within its territory.
questions.explanation: Historians generally point to a combination of causes.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Napoleon Bonaparte was
options: a French military leader who became emperor
questions.explanation: Napoleon rose during the French Revolution and became Emperor of the French.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Ninety-five Theses, which started the Reformation, were written by
questions.explanation: Martin Luther wrote the Ninety-five Theses in 1517.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Enlightenment, also called the Age of Reason, was an intellectual movement mainly of the
questions.explanation: It flourished in Europe mainly in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which thinker proposed the separation of powers in 'The Spirit of the Laws'?
questions.explanation: Montesquieu argued that legislative, executive and judicial powers should be separate.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The idea of separation of powers aims to
options: place all power in one person
prevent any single body from holding all power
questions.explanation: Dividing authority limits the chance of abuse.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Renaissance artists studied perspective and human anatomy. This shows
options: a greater interest in observing nature closely
a lack of interest in nature
questions.explanation: Close observation of nature marked Renaissance art and science.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What were the three Estates of French society before 1789?
questions.answer: The First Estate was the clergy, the Second Estate was the nobility, and the Third Estate was everyone else, including peasants, workers and the middle class.
questions.explanation: The Third Estate paid most taxes but had the least privilege.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how the American Revolution influenced events in France.
questions.answer: The American Declaration of Independence spread ideas of liberty and the rights of people, which interested French thinkers and citizens. France's help to the colonies also added to its debts, which deepened its financial crisis.
questions.explanation: Both ideas and finances linked the two events.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The innermost layer of the Earth is called the
questions.explanation: The core lies at the centre of the Earth.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara in northern Africa is the largest hot desert.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Mount Kilimanjaro is located in which continent?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro is in Tanzania, Africa.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Fossils are most commonly found in which type of rock?
questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks form in layers that can bury and preserve remains.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are fossils rarely found in igneous rocks?
options: The intense heat of molten rock destroys remains, while sediments bury them gently
questions.explanation: Molten material would destroy organic remains.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why do coasts near subduction zones face the risk of tsunamis?
options: Undersea earthquakes there can displace large volumes of water
questions.explanation: A sudden movement of the sea floor can set off large waves.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name the three main layers of the Earth's interior.
questions.answer: The crust, the mantle and the core. The core is further divided into an outer liquid part and an inner solid part.
questions.explanation: The layers differ in composition, temperature and state.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how glaciers shape the landscape.
questions.answer: Moving glaciers erode rock and scrape out deep, U-shaped valleys and basins. They carry the debris and drop it as moraines when they melt.
questions.explanation: Glacial erosion and deposition create distinctive landforms.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Clouds are formed by the
questions.explanation: Water vapour cools and condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which unit is commonly used to measure temperature in science and everyday life in India?
questions.explanation: Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which wind system brings most of India's summer rainfall?
questions.explanation: The southwest monsoon brings the main rainy season.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A cyclone is a weather system of
options: low pressure with winds spiralling inwards
questions.explanation: A cyclone has a low-pressure centre with winds blowing in a spiral around it.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are polar regions cold even though sunlight reaches them in summer?
options: The Sun's rays are slanting and much sunlight is reflected by snow and ice
They are close to the Sun
questions.explanation: Low angle of the rays and high reflection of ice limit warming.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A town at 3,000 metres altitude near the equator is cooler than a coastal town at the same latitude because
options: it is closer to the Sun
questions.explanation: Air temperature decreases with height in the troposphere.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: List the three main types of rainfall.
questions.answer: Convectional rainfall, relief or orographic rainfall, and cyclonic or frontal rainfall.
questions.explanation: Rainfall is classified by the way air is made to rise.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Describe the major relief features of the ocean floor.
questions.answer: Near the coast lies the gently sloping continental shelf, followed by the steep continental slope. Beyond are the flat abyssal plains, with mid-ocean ridges and deep trenches in places.
questions.explanation: The sea floor has mountains, plains and deep trenches like the land.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Fertile soil is rich in
questions.explanation: Humus and minerals supply nutrients to plants.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these animals is a herbivore?
questions.explanation: Cows feed on plants.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Decomposers such as fungi and bacteria
options: break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil
questions.explanation: Decomposers recycle nutrients from dead organisms.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which type of forest is typically found on higher, cooler mountain slopes such as parts of the Himalayas?
questions.explanation: Conifers such as pine and deodar grow in cooler highland areas.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Overuse of chemical fertilisers can harm soil because
options: they can upset soil life and nutrient balance and pollute water
they add large amounts of humus
they make soil fertile for ever
questions.explanation: Excessive use may damage soil organisms and run off into water bodies.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why do some animals migrate with the seasons?
options: To find food, water or a suitable climate
questions.explanation: Migration helps animals survive when conditions change.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name three types of natural vegetation and one region where each is found.
questions.answer: Tropical rainforest is found in the Amazon basin, tundra in the Arctic regions, and desert vegetation in the Sahara.
questions.explanation: Vegetation types follow climate patterns.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How can large-scale deforestation affect the water cycle and local climate?
questions.answer: Fewer trees mean less transpiration and less moisture in the air, which can reduce rainfall locally. Without roots to hold soil, runoff and soil erosion increase and groundwater recharge may fall.
questions.explanation: Forests help regulate water and climate.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The river Ganga finally flows into the
questions.explanation: The Ganga joins the Bay of Bengal after forming its delta.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Sundarbans mangrove forests lie in the delta of the
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans are in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Chilika Lake, a large coastal lagoon, is in which state?
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake lies on the coast of Odisha.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Aravalli range is one of the oldest fold mountain ranges of
questions.explanation: The Aravallis in north-western India are very old fold mountains.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Young Himalayan rivers cut deep gorges because
options: steep gradients give them great power to erode
questions.explanation: Fast flow on steep slopes gives strong downward erosion.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Konkan coast gets heavier monsoon rain than Pune because
options: Konkan lies on the windward side of the Western Ghats
Pune lies on the windward side
questions.explanation: Pune lies in the rain shadow on the leeward side.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: State two differences between Himalayan rivers and peninsular rivers.
questions.answer: Himalayan rivers are perennial as they are fed by snow and rain, while peninsular rivers are mostly seasonal. Himalayan rivers have long courses and large basins, while peninsular rivers are shorter and flow through older, stable land.
questions.explanation: Source and terrain explain the differences.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: State two causes and two effects of drought in India.
questions.answer: Causes include failure or delay of the monsoon and long gaps in rainfall. Effects include crop failure, shortage of drinking water and fodder, and loss of rural income.
questions.explanation: Drought is mainly a result of deficient monsoon rain.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: India is a
questions.explanation: The head of State is elected, not hereditary, so India is a republic.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The head of State of India is the
questions.explanation: The President is the constitutional head of State.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these women was a member of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: Hansa Mehta was one of the women members of the Assembly.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Constitution Day in India is observed on
questions.explanation: It marks the adoption of the Constitution on 26 November 1949.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A written Constitution is helpful in a federal system mainly because
options: it clearly lays down the powers of each level and helps settle disputes
questions.explanation: Written rules make the division of powers clear.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Constitution describes India as 'sovereign'. This means that India
options: has supreme authority over internal and external matters and is free from external control
questions.explanation: Sovereignty means independence in both internal and external matters.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is meant by a parliamentary system of government?
questions.answer: In a parliamentary system the executive is drawn from the legislature and is answerable to it. The head of State is nominal, while real power lies with the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers who must keep the confidence of the House.
keyPoints: nominal head of State and real head of government
questions.explanation: India follows this system at the Centre and in the States.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why must certain parts of the Constitution be amended only with the consent of the States?
questions.answer: Matters that affect the federal structure, such as the distribution of powers between the Union and the States, concern both levels. Requiring State consent, along with a special majority in Parliament, prevents the Centre from changing them alone.
keyPoints: federal matters concern both Centre and States
questions.explanation: Article 368 requires ratification by half the States for amendments to federal provisions.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which Article abolishes titles such as 'Raja' and 'Rai Bahadur'?
questions.explanation: Article 18 abolishes titles, other than military and academic distinctions.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Freedom of conscience belongs to which Fundamental Right?
questions.explanation: Articles 25 to 28 form the Right to Freedom of Religion.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A writ of quo warranto is issued to
options: release a person from unlawful detention
ask by what authority a person holds a public office
command an official to do a duty
questions.explanation: Quo warranto means 'by what authority'.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Under which Article can a person approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Article 32 gives the right to move the Supreme Court.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A newspaper is banned without any valid reason. Which right is most directly affected?
options: Freedom of speech and expression, which includes freedom of the press
questions.explanation: Freedom of the press is part of the freedom of speech and expression.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Voting regularly and holding governments accountable is an example of
questions.explanation: Active citizens take part in public life and monitor those in power.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How does being a citizen differ from being the subject of a king?
questions.answer: A citizen has equal rights, takes part in choosing the government and can question it, while a subject owes obedience to a ruler and has no equal political rights.
questions.explanation: Citizenship implies membership with rights and responsibilities in a political community.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the freedom of the press important in a democracy?
questions.answer: A free press informs citizens about the working of the government and public issues, which helps them take part and vote wisely. It also exposes wrongdoing, which makes those in power accountable.
questions.explanation: Information is essential for democratic decision-making.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The first general elections of independent India were held in
questions.explanation: The first general elections took place in 1951-52.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: EVM stands for
questions.explanation: EVMs are electronic devices for recording votes.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which authority audits the accounts of the Union and State governments?
questions.explanation: The CAG audits government accounts.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In the 'first-past-the-post' system, the winner in a constituency is the candidate who
options: gets more votes than any other candidate
gets an absolute majority of all voters
questions.explanation: The candidate with the highest number of votes wins, even without a majority.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are free and fair elections essential to democracy?
options: They let citizens choose and change governments peacefully
They end the need for laws
questions.explanation: Regular fair elections make governments accountable to the people.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is local self-government considered valuable in a democracy?
options: It brings decision-making on local matters closer to the people and eases participation
It reduces the say of citizens
questions.explanation: Local bodies let people take part in decisions that affect their daily lives.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: State two functions of the judiciary.
questions.answer: The judiciary settles disputes between citizens, and between citizens and the government, by interpreting and applying the law. It also protects the Fundamental Rights and can examine whether laws follow the Constitution.
questions.explanation: Courts apply laws and protect rights.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is it important that the Election Commission works independently?
questions.answer: An independent Commission can conduct elections fairly and without pressure from the government in power. This keeps voters' confidence in the result and the democratic process.
questions.explanation: Fair elections need an impartial authority.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Which of these is an example of discrimination?
options: Equal access to a public well
Denying a person entry to a public place because of caste
questions.explanation: Treating someone unfairly because of caste is discrimination.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: The ability to act and choose without unjust external restraint is called
questions.explanation: Liberty means freedom from unjust restraints.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: A system in which all adults have a say in choosing the government is called a
questions.explanation: In a democracy, citizens choose their rulers.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Political Concepts: Freedom, Equality and Justice
questions.q: Rights relating to food, shelter, health and education are mainly
questions.explanation: These rights relate to basic needs and living conditions.
